newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS official sees French sugar yield over 10 t/ha.
newsitem.headline: FIRS official sees French sugar yield over 10 t/ha.

text.p: Excellent growing conditions should push the national 1997/98 beet sugar yield well above 10 tonnes per hectare, an official for French sugar intervention board FIRS said on Thursday.
"Growing conditions are very good with a combination of rain and sun. Barring a climatic accident we should largely exceed 10 tonnes," the official told Reuters.
Last month FIRS predicted the crop would easily achieve a yield of 10 tonnes. Last season's yield was 10.01 tonnes.
In its July report due for release later this week, FIRS is expected to reinforce that forecast by saying a yield of 10 tonnes was now assured, the official said.
But FIRS will await the results of the first beet test scheduled in early August before making a more detailed forecast.

In its July report FIRS will also adjust upwards its estimate for area sown to sugar beets in 1997/98 to 421,000 hectares from a previous forecast of 420,000 hectares. This would compare with 1996/97 sowings of 422,000 hectares.
Last season France produced 4.226 million tonnes of beet sugar.
